summary: Gordon County lookout believed built in the 1940s and administered by the Georgia Forestry Commission; the latest report found from 2018 shows the cab removed.

facts.status_note: Standing at the May 2018 register visit, but the cab had been completely removed; no later condition report was found.

events.note: Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register August 28, 2017
Register visit report dated May 28, 2018 found the tower standing with the cab completely removed and the site overgrown

evidence.quote: This lookout is believed to have been built in the 1940s.

evidence.supports: Protects Calhoun and the surrounding area

evidence.quote: The tower is still standing, but is surrounded by junked vehicles, overgrown with poison ivy; and the cab has been completely removed.

evidence.supports: Steps completely overgrown with poison ivy vines
evidence.quote: The steps are completely overgrown with huge poison ivy vines.

evidence.supports: Visitor unsure whether site is public or private land
evidence.quote: Not sure if this is on public or private property??

evidence.supports: Georgia tower list codes it gfc-709 at elevation 906 (no units stated) in Gordon County

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 897 ft (273 m) and a Georgia tower list gives 906 with no units stated; read as feet to match the register, the difference is 9 ft. The record's 273.4 m matches the register and is kept.

notes_for_editor: One detailed source (the register entry with a May 2018 visitor report) and one tower list. No build year, design, staffing or current access status found. The visitor's note on public or private ownership is unresolved; a Gordon County or Georgia Forestry Commission contact is the best next step. Treat the 'standing' status as last confirmed in 2018.
